predecessors.name: Jin (Former Jin)
predecessors.text: Li Cunxu's Jin, which he turned into the Tang: 'in spring 923, Li Cunxu declared himself emperor of Tang' at Wei Prefecture

predecessors.name: Later Liang
predecessors.text: 'all of Later Liang territory' (Li Cunxu entered Daliang), without Gao Jixing's Jingnan

predecessors.name: Qi (Li Maozhen's state)
predecessors.text: Fengxiang Circuit, Li Maozhen's last ground, inherited by his son Li Jiyan as Tang military governor in 924

predecessors.name: Former Shu
predecessors.text: the Former Shu realm in Sichuan, surrendered to the Later Tang at the end of 925

successors.name: Later Jin
successors.text: the Later Tang realm without Sichuan and Hanzhong (Later Shu since 934); the Qin, Feng, Cheng and Jie prefectures (Xiongwu circuit) stay Later Tang land to the end

successors.name: Later Shu
successors.text: Sichuan with Hanzhong: the Xichuan and Dongchuan circuits under Meng Zhixiang and Shannan West, without the Qin/Feng/Cheng/Jie country

successors.name: Jingnan (Nanping)
successors.text: Gao Jixing's Jingnan, which 'would eventually, after Li Cunxu's death, effectively become independent of Later Tang'

ledger.x: 923: Li Cunxu proclaims the Tang at Daming.
923: Li Siyuan takes Yun Prefecture, Tianping's capital, in a surprise attack.
19 November 923: Li Cunxu takes Kaifeng and the Later Liang realm.
923: the Later Tang capital moves from Daming to Luoyang.
924: Qi submits to the Later Tang.
924: Gao Jixing is made Prince of Nanping by the Later Tang, and Jingnan is its dependency.
925: the Later Tang conquers the Former Shu.
927: Jingnan breaks with the Later Tang.
Spring 933: Meng Zhixiang is made Prince of Shu.
16 March 934: Meng Zhixiang proclaims the Later Shu.
16 March 934: Sichuan leaves the Later Tang.
Late 934 (September by the reign end): Hanzhong goes to the Later Shu.
936: Shi Jingtang rebels from Hedong and the Khitan make him emperor of the Later Jin.
11 January 937: Li Congke falls and the rest of the realm goes to Shi Jingtang.

wars.name: Later Tang destruction of Later Liang
wars.outcome: Li Cunxu took Kaifeng (surrender 19 November 923) and the whole Later Liang realm; the Later Liang ended.

wars.name: Later Tang conquest of Former Shu
wars.outcome: Li Jiji (titular) and Guo Chongtao attacked in late 925; Wang Yan surrendered the Former Shu realm by the end of 925.

wars.name: Later Tang campaign against Jingnan
wars.outcome: Mingzong declared a general campaign in spring 927; Fang Zhiwen was commissioned in fall 928; Gao Jixing died (late 928 or 28 January 929) and the campaign was ended in spring 929 with Jingnan under Gao Conghui, no land changing hands permanently on the pages.

wars.name: Later Tang campaign against Wang Du of Yiwu
wars.outcome: Wang Yanqiu besieged Ding Prefecture; the Khitan attempt to aid Wang Du failed and in early 929 his officer Ma Rangneng opened the gates; Wang Du killed himself and the Later Tang regained Yiwu.

wars.name: Dong Zhang's rebellion and Meng Zhixiang's independence of Sichuan
wars.outcome: Dong Zhang rebelled in fall 930 and was crushed in summer 932; Meng Zhixiang took Dongchuan, became Prince of Shu (933) and Emperor of Later Shu on 16 March 934.

wars.name: Later Tang expedition against Xia Prefecture (Dingnan)
wars.outcome: Li Yichao resisted Mingzong's transfer of the Dingnan command (An Congjin) and Yao Yanchou besieged Xia Prefecture in 933; the defence held, Li Yichao pled for forgiveness and the army withdrew; Dingnan thereafter showed the court no respect.

wars.name: Shi Jingtang's revolt against Later Tang
wars.outcome: Shi Jingtang, allied with the Khitan, overthrew Li Congke (11 January 937), founded the Later Jin and ceded the Sixteen Prefectures to the Liao.

certainty.note: Frontiers follow circuits and prefectures with no surveyed lines; the Khitan frontier in the north and the Tangut and Tibetan edge in the west are the softest.

sources.title: Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period
